Title: RM4bil needed annually to keep rural road projects on track
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Rural and Regional Development Ministry (KKDW) estimates that RM4 billion is needed annually to keep rural road projects nationwide on schedule.
The ministry said the estimate was based on existing commitments and funding required to ensure ongoing projects progressed smoothly.
As of Sept 1, 415 rural road projects were under way, involving RM1.995 billion, or 94 per cent, of this year's RM2.107 billion allocation.
"Based on current commitments, about RM4 billion is needed annually to ensure projects proceed smoothly and according to schedule.
"This reflects the active implementation of projects nationwide and the need to ensure ongoing works continue through to completion," it said in a statement.
The ministry said the programme involved development projects implemented in stages, with some taking several years to complete.
"Therefore, annual allocations must take into account ongoing projects as well as newly approved projects," it said.
KKDW said it would continue taking measures to ensure available funds were used effectively, with priority given to ongoing projects so their intended benefits could reach the people.
It also welcomed the Finance Ministry's approval of an additional RM300 million to meet the programme's immediate funding needs.
On Wednesday, the Finance Ministry said
no restrictions
had been imposed on KKDW's rural road allocation and that the approved funds had been fully disbursed.
It said payment constraints arose because this year's allocation was nearly exhausted.
The ministry also said KKDW had committed and spent more than its approved annual allocations in recent years.
Spending reached RM1.8 billion against an allocation of RM1.1 billion in 2023, RM2 billion against RM1.3 billion in 2024 and RM2.3 billion against RM1.6 billion last year.

Title: Zetrix AI scraps RM130mil MYEG Ventures deal over share price volatility
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd has called off its proposed RM130 million acquisition of a 50 per cent stake in Philippines-based MYEG Ventures Inc just three days after signing the deal, citing volatility in its share price.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, Zetrix AI said it terminated the share purchase agreement with Next Lion Ltd following a review of the deal's commercial rationale due to share price volatility affecting the consideration shares.
The termination comes after a sharp sell-off in Zetrix AI shares that began on Aug 27, when the counter closed at 59.5 sen, down nearly 10 per cent from 66 sen a day earlier.
The stock then plunged 30 sen, or 50.42 per cent, to 29.5 sen on Aug 28, before falling further to 25 sen on Sept 1 — the same day Zetrix AI signed the RM130 million deal with Next Lion.
Zetrix AI shares fell another 30 per cent to 17.5 sen on Sept 2, taking their decline from the Aug 26 close of 66 sen to 73.48 per cent in just four trading days.
The stock has since rebounded for two consecutive sessions, closing at 25.5 sen today.
Under the agreement, Zetrix AI was to acquire 15.25 million shares, representing a 50 per cent stake in MYEG Ventures, from Next Lion for RM130 million.
The purchase consideration was to be satisfied through a combination of cash and the issuance of up to 360.57 million new Zetrix AI shares.
The issue price of the consideration shares was to be based on the five-day volume-weighted average market price of Zetrix AI shares immediately preceding their issuance.
The remaining consideration, after deducting the value of the consideration shares, would have been paid in cash using internally generated funds.
Zetrix AI said neither party would incur any break fees or penalties from the termination, with both released from further obligations under the agreement.
The company said the termination would have no material impact on its paid-up share capital, substantial shareholders' shareholdings, earnings per share, consolidated net assets per share or gearing.
Its board said the termination was in the best interest of the company.

Title: King attends first semi final match of Johor Super Crown Polo tournament
Article:
JOHOR BARU: His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today graced the first semi-final polo match of the Johor Super Crown Polo Tournament (JSCPT) 2026.
According to a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar's official Facebook page, His Majesty was accompanied by the Regent of Johor, Tunku Mahkota Ismail.
The first semi-final, featuring Temasek and Korea Polo, was held at the Royal Johor Polo Ground, Istana Pasir Pelangi, here this morning.
The tournament features a 22-goal handicap competition, which is the highest level ever staged in Malaysia.
The organisation of the tournament is driven by the joint vision of Tunku Mahkota Ismail and world polo icon Pablo "Polito" Pieres to position Johor as a key destination on the international polo circuit.
Five elite teams - Royal Johor, Temasek, JCorp, Korea Polo and Digital Bridge - are taking part, featuring a line-up of world-class international players, including several who have won the Argentine Open on multiple occasions.

Title: Azalina calls for red flags, warning signs at high-risk Desaru beaches
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: Pengerang member of Parliament Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said has called for coastal areas in Desaru, including Pantai Tanjung Lompat, to be equipped with red flags and warning signs to deter people from swimming in high-risk areas.
She said she had proposed the measure to the local authorities, particularly for beaches with strong currents that are unsuitable for swimming.
"This is important, especially during the school holidays when more visitors are expected to visit the beaches," she told a press conference after visiting the family of a drowning victim at Pantai Tanjung Lompat today.
Azalina, who is also Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform), advised families to avoid sea activities from September to December due to strong winds.
She said visitors might not be aware of the risks, particularly at campsites without clear signs prohibiting swimming.
On the need for beach patrol or lifeguards, Azalina said the matter should be studied as the coastline in Pengerang is extensive and would involve additional costs, unlike resorts where lifeguards are part of the management.
She said sea conditions in Pengerang differ from those in several other coastal areas such as Terengganu, Mersing and Tioman, as the area is a trade route with strong currents.
She said strong winds can also cause the sea to appear calm on the surface even when it is unsafe, as there may be strong or swirling currents beneath the water.
Three of the four victims in Wednesday morning's incident have so far been found drowned. They were Muhammad Adib Hafiy Kamal, Muhammad Thaqif Rayyan Rumainoor and Alif Taqiuddin Kamal Hasrul, all aged 16.
The search for the fourth victim, Mohamad Haiman Fitri Supian, who remains missing, is ongoing.

Title: Excel Force co-founder Wang returns as substantial shareholder after seven years
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Excel Force MSC Bhd co-founder and former managing director Wang Kuen-Chung has returned as a substantial shareholder of the company, seven years after relinquishing that status and stepping down from its helm.
Wang acquired 73.31 million Excel Force shares via the open market on Sept 1, followed by another 10 million shares a day later, taking his direct holding to 89.31 million shares, or 14.645 per cent.
The shares added to the six million shares he already held, according to Bursa Malaysia filings today. No prices were disclosed.
The Taiwanese businessman's return as a substantial shareholder coincided with a reshuffle of Excel Force's board, with the company announcing the appointment of three new directors.
Excel Force is currently chaired by Datuk Seri Farhash Wafa Salvador, the former political secretary to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim who has in recent years built up corporate interests across several Bursa Malaysia-listed companies.
Farhash was appointed to Excel Force's board in May 2023 and currently serves as its executive chairman. He is also executive chairman of Apex Equity Holdings Bhd and Key Alliance Group Bhd.
Excel Force today appointed Teo Beng Wei and Sylvan Sim Chi Meng as independent non-executive directors and Goh Jooi Shen as executive director.
The three new directors have overlapping corporate links. Teo and Sylvan are directors of Cuscapi Bhd, while Goh sits on the board of SerSol Bhd alongside Teo.
MyBursa data showed Zetrix AI Bhd managing director Wong Thean Soon as Excel Force's largest shareholder with a 24.32 per cent stake, although the shareholder list has yet to reflect Wang's latest acquisitions.
Wang had ceased to be a substantial shareholder of Excel Force on Feb 22, 2019, after Exacta Co Ltd, through which he held an indirect interest, disposed of 1.90 million shares via the open market.
The disposal reduced his indirect interest to 17.22 million shares, or 4.155 per cent, while his direct holding stood at 1.90 million shares, or 0.458 per cent, Bursa filings showed.
Exacta subsequently sold a total of 1.60 million shares, reducing Wang's indirect holding to 15.62 million shares, or 3.769 per cent.
Wang, who co-founded the company with his wife in 1994, subsequently retired as Excel Force's managing director on July 23, 2019.
Listed on the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia, Excel Force provides application solutions for the stockbroking and financial services industry.

Title: HHRG appoints Syed Azman as executive chairman
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: HHRG Bhd has appointed Tan Sri Syed Azman Syed Ibrahim as executive chairman effective today.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the manufacturer and trader of biomass material said Syed Azman holds a doctorate in engineering from Universiti Putra Malaysia. He began his career in the Royal Intelligence Corps of the Malaysian Armed Forces and served for 30 years before retiring as a major in 1994.
The filing said he subsequently started his business career in the automotive sector, selling imported cars before securing franchises for global brands including Honda, Chevrolet, Ford, Smart, Audi and Suzuki.
"Today, his automotive portfolio includes Weststar Auto, a leading Honda dealership in Malaysia, Weststar Motors, which specialises in imported luxury cars, and Weststar Maxus, a prominent distributor of commercial vehicles nationwide," the company said.
In 2002, he founded Weststar Aviation Services, a provider of offshore helicopter transportation services operating across Asia, Europe, the Middle East and Africa.
HHRG added that Syed Azman is also an independent trustee of the Jeffrey Cheah Foundation.
Syed Azman has no family relationship with any HHRG director or major shareholder.

Title: 2 houses and 9 vehicles destroyed in fire at Durian Tunggal
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Nine vehicles were destroyed after two semi-permanent semi-detached houses caught fire in Kampung Padang Keladi, Durian Tunggal today.
Melaka Fire and Rescue Department Assistant Operations Division director Mohd Shahrom Laji said the nine vehicles included two cars, six motorcycles - including one electric motorcycle - and an electric bicycle.
"The fire department received an emergency call at 1.16pm before deploying a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT) and a Compact Fire Rescue Tender (CFRT), with a strength of seven personnel, along with two Rapid Intervention Motorcycle (RIM) units to the scene about a minute later.
"Upon arriving at the scene, two semi-permanent semi-detached houses measuring 35 x 70 sqft were found to be 100 percent and 80 percent burned, respectively," he said in a statement here today.
He said no casualties were reported and the fire was completely extinguished by 4pm.

Title: Pulau Redang coral reef damage under scrutiny, Terengganu to engage stakeholders
Article:
KUALA NERUS: The Terengganu government will hold an engagement session next week with vari9ious quarters, including representatives from the Department of Fisheries Malaysia, tourism operators and researchers, to discuss coral reef damage at Pulau Redang.
State Tourism, Culture, Environment and Climate Change Committee chairman Datuk Razali Idris said the session, scheduled from Sept 7 to 9, is crucial to obtaining an accurate assessment of the condition of the coral reefs and identifying the best measures to ensure the continued preservation and sustainability of the island's marine ecosystem.
He said the discussions would cover issues including boat relocation and operations, as well as proposals to limit the number of tourists and diving activities.
"We will examine all relevant issues. If we do not take care of this now, I am convinced that in another 20 to 25 years, Pulau Redang will be nothing more than an island; its beauty and underwater attractions could be lost forever.
"I will be there personally for three days to dive and inspect the condition of the coral reefs, which are reported to have suffered severe damage," he said after the flag-off ceremony for the Terengganu Merdeka Challenge at Bandar Baru today.
However, Razali said preliminary information from the Fisheries Department indicated that the extent of coral reef damage at the resort island remained manageable, although ongoing restoration efforts were necessary.
He said the damage to coral reefs at Pulau Redang, including in several marine park areas, was attributed to natural factors rather than tourism activities, as alleged by various quarters.
Nevertheless, he said the state government would consider proposals to introduce new guidelines if additional control measures were deemed necessary to protect and preserve the coral reef ecosystem.
"In places such as marine parks, outsiders are not permitted to enter. The damage is caused by environmental factors such as changes in currents, hot weather, climate change and the like.
"I feel it is inappropriate to simply point fingers at divers or boat operators. According to the department, the damage is largely due to environmental factors," he said.

Title: Explainer: What the Serian haze emergency means
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A haze emergency is the highest level under Malaysia's Air Pollutant Index (API) classification and applies when the reading exceeds 500.
According to the Department of Environment (DoE), pollution at this level is dangerous to high-risk groups and the general public, who must follow instructions issued by the authorities and monitor official announcements.
The declaration allows coordinated measures under the National Haze Action Plan, including the closure of non-essential workplaces, suspension of outdoor activities, intensified health monitoring and enforcement against activities that could worsen air pollution.
The emergency declared in Serian is a localised disaster measure aimed at protecting the public from extremely hazardous air pollution, not a nationwide emergency or security lockdown.
Why was an emergency declared?
Under the National Haze Action Plan, a haze emergency may be declared when the API reaches 500 or higher.
Serian
crossed that threshold today, with the monitoring station at the district police headquarters recording an API reading of 521 at 2pm.
The DoE classifies API readings of between 301 and 500 as hazardous, while readings above 500 are categorised as an emergency.
Does it cover all of Sarawak?
No. The declaration applies only to Serian and does not place the whole of Sarawak or Malaysia under emergency measures.
Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas had previously said any declaration would be confined to the locality where the API crossed the emergency threshold.
What will close?
Government and private-sector offices and workplaces in Serian may be ordered to close, with non-essential activities suspended.
During the 2013 haze emergency in Muar and Ledang, factories, estates and construction sites were closed, while the use of private vehicles was restricted.
Schools, kindergartens and childcare centres had already been required to close when the API exceeded 200 under the National Haze Action Plan.
What remains open?
Essential services will continue operating.
During the 2013 emergency, these included healthcare, fire and rescue, water and electricity supplies, telecommunications, postal services, transport, ports, fuel supplies, banking and finance, and services directly involved in managing the haze disaster.
The authorities are expected to specify which exemptions apply in Serian.
What does it mean for residents?
The declaration does not automatically impose a curfew or change the way the federal or state governments are administered.
However, residents should remain indoors as far as possible, keep doors and windows closed and avoid strenuous outdoor activity.
Those who must leave home should use a properly fitted particulate respirator such as an N95 mask. Children, older people, pregnant women and those with respiratory or cardiovascular illnesses should take additional precautions.
How long will it last?
The emergency will remain in force until it is formally withdrawn.
Authorities will continue monitoring the API, weather conditions and public health risks before deciding when the measures can be lifted.
The 2013 declaration in Muar and Ledang in Johor was similarly imposed until API readings returned to safer levels.
Has Malaysia declared haze emergencies before?
Yes. Haze emergencies were previously declared in Sarawak in 1997, Kuala Selangor and Port Klang in 2005, and Muar and Ledang in Johor in 2013.

Title: ByteDance secures $29.6 billion loan in AI push, sources say
Article:
HONG KONG: ByteDance has secured a US$29.6 billion loan from nearly 30 banks, three people with direct knowledge of the matter said on Friday, with the Chinese social media giant's bet on AI development driving strong interest from lenders.
The loan is the second-largest made in Asia this year after SoftBank raised US$40 billion in March to boost OpenAI investments, underscoring lenders' enthusiasm for the sector which demands ever-increasing capital.
Chinese, U.S., European and Singaporean banks are participating in the financing, the people said, with the three-year loan co-ordinated by Citigroup and JPMorgan set to be signed by ByteDance shortly.
ByteDance and JPMorgan did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Citi declined to comment. Bloomberg News first reported on the loan on Thursday.
The owner of popular social media apps Douyin and TikTok increased the facility from an initial target of US$20 billion after an overwhelming response from lenders, said the people, who declined to be named as the information was confidential.
Chinese banks have subscribed to more than 60 per cent of the total amount, one of them added.
ByteDance told lenders the financing would be for general corporate purposes, but the people said that the funds will mainly support the company's AI-related plans.
The facility has an initial term of three years and options to extend for two more years, two of them said.
RARE UNSECURED MEGA LOAN
ByteDance has stepped up its AI spending. Reuters reported in June that the tech firm was in talks with Shanghai-based Iluvatar ‌CoreX to purchase AI chips for inference work and is also considering a similar deal with Baidu .
The new dollar-denominated facility is unsecured, meaning ByteDance is not pledging any asset or shares as collateral, reflecting how confidently lenders view the company's creditworthiness.
"It is very rare to see such a mega loan unsecured," said one of the sources. "The banks practically are counting purely on ByteDance's name."
The loan will be used to fund projects outside China, the source said, adding ByteDance is the offtaker for many of the data centers being built in Southeast Asia. An offtaker signs a binding contract with a data center to purchase a certain amount of its capacity.
"ByteDance is competing with local hyperscalers on AI data centers and with global hyperscalers on multimodal AI model," said Lian Jye Su, chief analyst at research firm Omdia.
"Both require massive investment, especially if we look at the Capex poured into AI training by the likes of OpenAI and Google," he said.
ByteDance last tapped the global loan market in September 2024, raising US$10.8 billion from roughly 20 international and Chinese lenders, according to a Bloomberg report at the time.

Title: Nepal's 'Himalayan tsunami': What we know
Article:
KATHMANDU: Nepal is reeling from a deadly Himalayan glacial mountain collapse on the border with China that has killed more than 1,300 people and left upwards of 5,600 missing in both countries.
Scientists have been examining the August 26 catastrophe, dubbed a "Himalayan tsunami" by Nepal's foreign minister.
Here is what experts – including from the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) and the HiRISK group, focusing on Asia's mountains – have deciphered so far.
- WHAT HAPPENED? -
On Aug 26 at 8.37am (0252 GMT), a mass of ice and rock broke away from the north face of Nepal's Langtang Lirung mountain, sending a huge mass of debris racing down the valley.
The collapse began at an altitude of about 5,200 metres with a section more than a kilometre wide and extending roughly 700 metres vertically, according to ICIMOD.
That mass of rock and ice plunged about 800 metres onto a debris-covered glacier, before surging downhill, briefly damming the Lhende River. Water and debris then burst downstream.
The debris travelled about 20 kilometres, dropping 1,700 metres at Rasuwagadhi in only seven minutes, ICIMOD geologist Sudan Bikash Maharjan told AFP.
"The elevation difference is high, within a very short length," Maharjan said. "So it just rushed down like a bullet train."
The collapse swept up vast quantities of loose material as it descended, helping create an exceptionally destructive and fast-moving flow.
Experts are still investigating the large volume of water that allowed the debris to travel far downstream.
It also created two lakes. One has slowly drained. Experts believe the second one will not cause a high-magnitude flood.
- WHY DID THE MOUNTAIN COLLAPSE? -
Experts say several factors may have contributed, but it is too early to identify a single trigger.
The glacier in the area retreated by about 450 metres between 1990 and 2020, exposing rock that had previously been covered by ice.
Changes in temperature, moisture and permafrost may have weakened fractures in the exposed rock, while water entering cracks could have helped destabilise the slope.
But there was no earthquake, exceptional rainfall or sudden period of extreme heat immediately before the collapse, experts said.
"To pinpoint 'this is the cause', we need to go to the field, do the analysis," Maharjan said.
A major earthquake in 2015 may also have contributed to longer-term instability. But experts are examining whether cracks may have developed in the mountain over a longer period.
- WAS ROLE DOES CLIMATE CHANGE PLAY? -
Climate change may have contributed to conditions that made the slope more vulnerable, but experts caution against attributing the disaster solely to rising temperatures.
Warming has accelerated glacier retreat across the Himalayas, exposing previously ice-covered rock to changing temperatures and water conditions.
Permafrost degradation may also weaken mountain slopes and allow water to penetrate deeper into fractures.
"Climate change makes all this more likely," geoscientist Jakob Steiner said, while noting that mountain collapses are also part of natural geological processes.
- COULD IT HAVE BEEN PREDICTED? -
Scientists are examining possible warning signs, including evidence that the glacier accelerated in the weeks before the collapse, and a sudden increase in meltwater shortly beforehand.
But neither was enough to predict with certainty that a catastrophic collapse was imminent.
Steiner said the analysis should not suggest that authorities in Nepal or China would have known the mountain was about to fail.
"There are so many mountains in the region," he said.
- WHAT MAY HELP PREVENT SIMILAR DISASTERS? -
Experts hope that understanding the events of Aug 26 will lead to the development of tools capable of predicting a recurrence.
"We are using... this knowledge now to be better prepared in future – to find tools that let us focus in on that 'one needle in the haystack', that we actually need to pay attention to," Steiner told AFP.
Experts say better long-term monitoring, data sharing and coordination are crucial.
"We really need a dedicated mechanism... which works around the clock," disaster specialist Saswata Sanyal told AFP.--AFP

Title: RM4.25mil project to ease flash floods in Kampung Pokok Asam
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A RM4.25 million flood mitigation project at Parit Monsun, Kampung Pokok Asam is expected to improve drainage capacity and reduce flash floods.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the project, which began on July 26, 2024, was crucial to addressing flooding in the low-lying area, which frequently experiences excess water during heavy rain.
He said although fewer than 20 houses were typically affected during each flood, mitigation measures were necessary to improve protection and minimise disruption to residents.
"The project is expected to reduce flash floods that occur several times a year, particularly during heavy rain and high tides.
"However, we cannot promise a 100 per cent solution as every project has capacity limitations based on its design and the size of the catchment involved," he said during a site visit near Lintang Tengku, Jelutong, here today.
Chow said the project was now in its final stage and expected to be completed in October.
The project includes a pump house equipped with two screw pumps, each with a capacity of 1.0 cubic metre per second, along with a monsoon drain diversion, a new culvert and related infrastructure.
"The screw pumps were chosen as they are more suitable for the area compared with submersible pumps, particularly in reducing disruptions caused by rubbish that could affect pump operations.
"With the pump house, water from the monsoon drain can be discharged more efficiently, especially during heavy rain and high tides," he added.
The project also involves a 12m-long monsoon drain diversion measuring 3m by 3.6m, connecting the existing drain to the screw pumps, as well as a 15m-long, 750mm by 750mm culvert.
Chow, who is also Padang Kota assemblyman, said the project was part of the state government's efforts with the Penang Drainage and Irrigation Department (DID) to improve drainage capacity and reduce flood risks in vulnerable areas.
Kampung Pokok Asam was previously identified as a flood hotspot, with flash floods occurring annually and requiring mobile pumps during heavy rain and high tides.
Rapid development has also altered surface water flows, while the existing drainage system is no longer sufficient to cope with higher water volumes.

Title: Man returns to Kelantan for Pas Muktamar, learns cyclist brother killed in crash
Article:
KOTA BARU: A man who had just returned from Selangor to attend the 72nd Pas Muktamar here was left devastated after learning that his younger brother was among two best friends killed when a car crashed into them while they were cycling today.
Private-sector worker Zamri Risman Mahmet, 52, said he received a call from his younger brother and uncle about 10.30am informing him that his 49-year-old brother, Zamrie Rismawadi, had been killed in the accident.
[[nid:1525762]]
"I arrived from Selangor last night to attend the Pas Muktamar in Pengkalan Chepa.
"I received the call while at the Muktamar about 10.30am and was told that my brother had died in the accident," he said when met at Raja Perempuan Zainab II Hospital's forensic unit.
Zamri said he immediately rushed to the scene, where other family members had gathered after being informed of the tragedy.
"When I arrived at the scene, I saw my brother's body on the road shoulder while the other victim was in a drain.
"I was told that my brother was cycling with his friend when the incident occurred.
"My brother was in front while his friend was behind. Following the crash, his bicycle was scattered on the road," he said.
Zamri said his brother was the second of 11 siblings and had been an avid cyclist since his teenage years.
"He regularly went cycling, exercising or riding a motorcycle with his friends, usually every week.
"He had even told us that he planned to cycle to Thailand with his group after this."
Zamri said he last met his brother about two months ago.
He added that his return to Kelantan as a member of Persatuan Anak Kelantan (Perakan), which had invited him to attend the Muktamar, was an opportunity for him to meet his brother.
Zamri said his brother's remains would be buried at Kota Seribong Cemetery here tonight.
It was reported that
two cyclists
were killed when they were hit by a car at Km18 of the Kota Baru-Ketereh Highway here this morning.
Zamrie and another victim, Nik Zaki Yamani Nik Abdul Aziz, 49, died on the spot in the 8.30am crash.

Title: Ringgit ends lower against US dollar as US rate hike debate persists
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit finished lower against the US dollar on Friday as the market closely monitors the ongoing debate regarding interest rate hikes in the United States.
This comes ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting scheduled for September 15 and 16. The US Federal Reserve (Fed) has kept interest rates unchanged so far in 2026, but hawkish remarks by Fed Chair Kevin Warsh at the Jackson Hole symposium have increased expectations of a rate hike this month.
At 6 pm, the ringgit was quoted at 4.0425/0465 against the US dollar compared with Thursday's close of 4.0405/0445.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit was fairly stable despite market uncertainties.
Against a basket of major currencies, the ringgit dipped against the euro to 4.6962/7008 from yesterday's 4.6894/6940 and eased against the British pound to 5.4663/4717 from 5.4539/4593.
The local note also weakened against the Japanese yen to 2.5832/5860 from 2.5838/5865 at Thursday's close.
The ringgit traded mostly lower against regional currencies.
It inched up against the Philippine peso at 6.45/6.46 from 6.46/6.47 yesterday and declined against the Singapore dollar to 3.1888/1923 from 3.1850/1884.
It fell against the Thai baht to 12.2693/2863 from 12.2421/2598 and also traded lower against the Indonesian rupiah at 229.1/229.4 from 228.5/228.8 at yesterday's close.

Title: Haze persists nationwide, Serian remains worst-hit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Haze continues to affect several parts of the country this evening, with Serian, Sarawak, remaining the worst-hit area.
As of 6pm, two of 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide recorded hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, according to the Department of Environment's API Management System.
Serian, which is under a haze emergency, recorded an API reading of 515, up from 400 at the same time yesterday, while Kuching recorded 306.
Two locations in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy readings – Samarahan (292) and Sri Aman (241).
Another 14 locations recorded unhealthy readings, including Sarikei (183), Sibu (182), Mukah (177), Bintulu (161), Samalaju (155), ILP Miri (154) and Miri (116) in Sarawak; Tawau (153), Politeknik Kota Kinabalu (151) and Sandakan (120) in Sabah; and Pasir Gudang (152), Larkin (142), Kota Tinggi (142) and Segamat (116) in Johor.
Elsewhere, 37 monitoring stations recorded moderate air quality, while 13 recorded good readings.
An API reading of 0-50 indicates good air quality, 51-100 moderate, 101-200 unhealthy, 201-300 very unhealthy and readings above 300 hazardous.
The haze, linked to fires that have burned for weeks in Indonesia's Kalimantan and Sumatra regions, has crossed borders and deteriorated air quality in parts of Malaysia, particularly Sarawak.
Sarawak has also reported an
increase
in acute respiratory tract infections and conjunctivitis amid the worsening haze.
Earlier, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, consented to the declaration of a
haze emergency
in Serian following the deterioration in air quality.

Title: Haze threatens ecosystems, wildlife populations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Transboundary haze not only threatens human health, but also has a long-term effect on the survival of ecosystems and wildlife populations due to habitat destruction and disruption of the respiratory system.
Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) Environmental Governance expert Assoc Prof Dr Haliza Abdul Rahman said among the significant impacts on fauna were chronic respiratory damage, decreased reproduction rates, dehydration and lack of food sources.
The UPM head of Laboratory Institute for Social Science Studies also said that large mammals and primates such as orangutans in Borneo and Sumatra, for example, faced the threat of respiratory tract infections following forest fires, which also affected the availability of their food sources.
"The haze does not only affect humans, but also animals and plants.
"Toxic smoke also disrupts the life cycles of pollinating insects such as bees and fireflies, while affecting the availability of food for fruit-eating animals such as hornbills," she said as a guest on Bernama Radio's 'Fokus 30' programme here today.
Haliza said thick haze also reduced visibility for wildlife, resulting in a higher risk of these animals straying from their natural habitats into forest fringes or human settlements.
"When animals flee from fires or are trapped in thick haze, they lose energy due to dehydration and starvation. A lack of water and food weakens animals such as deer and tapirs," she said.
She said the situation indirectly increased the risk of wildlife becoming easy targets for poachers, especially when enforcement was more focused on firefighting operations and managing the haze crisis.
To reduce these risks, Haliza proposed the setting up of a multi-agency rapid response team involving the Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan), the Fire and Rescue Department and non-governmental organisations (NGOs).
She also suggested the implementation of wildlife rescue and relocation protocols, the construction of emergency migration corridors, as well as the use of an early warning system based on artificial intelligence (AI) and air quality sensors in forest reserve areas.
The entire Serian Division in Sarawak was declared a disaster emergency following hazardous haze conditions, with the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading reaching 514 as of 4pm today.
His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, consented to the declaration of an
emergency
after considering advice from Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg and relevant agencies on air quality in the area.

Title: Nepali foreman rescued after nine days says he stayed behind to save others
Article:
KATHMANDU: When the mountain gave way above the Nepali power plant where Sanjay Sah worked, he had a choice: flee, or stay. He chose to stay and help.
The mechanical foreman was rescued on Friday alongside another worker, nine days after a wall of ice, rock and debris levelled the valley where the Upper Trishuli 3A Hydropower Station was located, providing a rare glimmer of hope in search operations for thousands missing after the unprecedented disaster.
"I was in the control room in the tunnel. Normally there are four to six people there, but there could have been 40 to 45 people that day," the 30-year-old told army officials from a stretcher, an oxygen mask strapped to his face, in a video shared by the Nepali authorities.
"My responsibility was to save everyone's lives. When there was such a big accident, it was not right for me to run away."
Sah said he had warned the others the moment word came of the disaster upstream, urging them to flee. He never made it out himself. By the time he turned to run, there was no time left.
Officials believe at least 900 people are trapped in tunnels related to six hydropower projects along the Trishuli river.
For nine days, Sah sat in the tunnel's darkness, where he chanted mantras (verses from a prayer) to hold onto hope. He managed to stay in contact with three or four other workers somewhere in the tunnel and said others could be trapped deeper into the mountain.
Sah and fellow survivor Kabir Maharjan, a mechanical supervisor, are the first workers to be rescued from the hydropower projects. A small group had managed to escape from another tunnel hours after the disaster struck.
Footage released by the Nepali Army showed Sah being carried out on a worker's back, his face caked in mud.
At least 1,287 people were killed in Nepal as houses, streets and schools in towns and villages near the border with China's Tibet were swept away. So far 5,083 people are reported missing and thousands more displaced. China has put the death toll in Tibet at 21, with 541 others listed as missing.
Sah and Maharjan have been taken to an army hospital in Kathmandu, where they remain in intensive care.--REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 647 Sarawak schools to close for 5 days over haze
Article:
KUCHING: A total of 647 schools in Sarawak will be closed for five days from Sept 7 to 11 due to haze and unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in several areas.
The closures involve 563 primary schools with 108,477 pupils and 84 secondary schools with 90,082 students under 12 district education offices.
Sarawak Education director Omar Mahli said the department prioritised the welfare, health and safety of students, particularly amid hot weather and unpredictable conditions.
"Based on continuous monitoring of API readings during the school holidays and reports issued by the Malaysian Meteorological Department, the Sarawak Education Department has decided to temporarily close the affected schools.
"This is to prioritise the health and safety of students and the entire education community," he said in a statement today.
The affected schools are under the Kuching, Padawan, Bau, Lundu, Samarahan, Simunjan, Serian, Sri Aman, Lubok Antu, Kanowit, Julau and Meradong district education offices.
Omar said home-based teaching and learning (PdPR) would be implemented throughout the closure.
He said the measure was in line with Education Ministry Circular Letter No. 8 of 2016 on guidelines for managing teaching and learning during disasters.
Any changes to the closure period or latest developments would be announced from time to time, while schools must comply with all prescribed standard operating procedures and guidelines, he added.
Omar also advised schools to refer to Education Ministry Circular Letter No. 1 of 2019 on measures to safeguard students' health and safety in schools located in areas with critical haze conditions.
"All education institutions under the Sarawak Education Department are also advised to comply with the guidelines on outdoor activities at Education Ministry institutions during hot weather and continuously monitor API readings through the Air Pollutant Index Management System.
"Education institutions must remain vigilant and follow Health Ministry advice to safeguard the health, safety and well-being of students, teachers and the entire education community," he said.

Title: Nicol David among eight honoured with 2026 Merdeka Award
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Eight Malaysians and organisations whose work spans humanitarian relief, conservation, science, academia and sports have been named recipients of the 2026 Merdeka Award.
Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) president and group chief executive officer Tengku Tan Sri Muhammad Taufik said the award embodied the "Spirit of Merdeka" by recognising individuals and organisations whose work had made a difference to Malaysia and improved the lives of Malaysians.
[[nid:1525771]]
He said the achievements of the Merdeka Award laureates served as a reminder that transformational contributions were not necessarily the work of extraordinary people, but often came from ordinary individuals driven by extraordinary missions.
"Behind these monumental and transformational achievements are individuals not too different from you and me.
"They are also ordinary individuals who have realised extraordinary pursuits. These ordinary individuals are, however, charged with extraordinary missions.
"Such missions were matched by their sheer courage and their audacity to pursue new possibilities," he said in his welcome address at the 2026 Merdeka Award ceremony.
The prestigious awards were presented by the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah, who is also Royal Patron and Chairman of the Merdeka Award Trust.
Mercy Malaysia received the Outstanding Contribution to Education & Community award for its emergency humanitarian assistance and relief efforts in Malaysia and more than 35 countries.
Professor Dr Chan Eng Heng was recognised under the Outstanding Contribution to Environment & Planetary Health category for her lifelong work in safeguarding Malaysia's turtle populations and advancing marine conservation.
Former world squash champion Datuk Nicol Ann David received the Outstanding Contribution to Humanities, Arts & Sports award for raising Malaysia's profile in world squash and inspiring young people through youth empowerment.
The Outstanding Contribution to Science, Technology & Innovation award was jointly conferred on Prof Datin Paduka Setia Datuk Dr Aini Ideris and Prof Datuk Dr Asma Ismail.
Dr Aini was recognised for pioneering veterinary innovations that strengthened food security and animal health, while Dr Asma was honoured for her transformative contributions to Malaysia's higher education and scientific innovation ecosystem.
Linguist Datuk Dr Asmah Omar received the Outstanding Scholastic & Academic Achievement award for her lifelong contribution to documenting, preserving and advancing Malaysia's linguistic heritage.
Meanwhile, Dr Omar Abdul Rahman was named recipient of the Anugerah Khas Merdeka for his pivotal role in shaping Malaysia's science, technology and innovation landscape.
Cheah received the Anugerah Harapan Merdeka for elevating Malaysia's standing in global para-badminton and inspiring persons with disabilities through sporting excellence.
With this year's recipients, the Merdeka Award has now recognised 78 individuals and organisations since its inaugural presentation in 2008.

Title: Felda cooperative to pay share withdrawals in stages, prioritise critical cases
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Payments for share withdrawal applications by Koperasi Permodalan Felda Malaysia Bhd (KPF) members will be made in stages and on a rotational basis, with priority given to special and critical cases.
KPF said these included medical expenses, education, property matters, haj, umrah and other religious needs, subject to sufficient cash flow.
"KPF acknowledges that there are still outstanding share withdrawal applications that have yet to be paid. KPF understands members' concerns and their need to access their shares to meet financial needs and sustain their livelihoods," it said in a statement.
The cooperative said a sharp increase in share withdrawal applications over the past five years had put pressure on its cash flow.
It said efforts were under way to restructure and dispose of identified investment assets to meet the claims. Some of these efforts were successfully concluded in 2025, with the proceeds used to facilitate share withdrawal payments.
Despite liquidity constraints, KPF said the group's business operations remained positive, supported by plantations, corporate investments, property, capital markets, Ar-Rahnu and financing.
KPF is also in the process of distributing RM102.1 million in dividends for 2025.
It said its investment asset rationalisation plan would be implemented strategically and progressively to strengthen its financial position and ensure business continuity.
The cooperative said the plan also took into account members' needs and interests, particularly in fulfilling share withdrawal applications.
"KPF appreciates the patience, trust and continued support of all members and assures them that the management of share withdrawal payments will continue to be carried out in a transparent and orderly manner."
Earlier today, KPF
members hit out
at delays in share redemption payments amounting to millions of ringgit.
The delays have reportedly affected more than 9,000 members nationwide.
More than 30 affected members staged a peaceful demonstration and hunger strike outside Balai Felda in Jalan Gurney 1, demanding an immediate resolution.

Title: MACC suspends orange garbs for remand detainees
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has suspended, with immediate effect, the requirement for persons under investigation to wear its orange uniform when brought to court for remand proceedings.
The move comes after Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said earlier today that political leaders would be given leeway not to wear the MACC orange uniform when brought to court.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the decision was made following recent developments and current recommendations concerning procedures for handling persons under investigation, particularly when they are brought to court.
"Persons under investigation will be allowed to wear their own clothes when brought to court, while lock-up attire will only be worn throughout the period they are held in the lock-up," he said in a statement today.
Abd Halim said the use of handcuffs would depend on the circumstances of each case.
He said exemptions would be given to those who were infirm, persons with disabilities, children and senior citizens.
"However, MACC will continue to take precautionary measures and ensure that appropriate security controls are implemented throughout the handling of persons under investigation."
He said the commission remained committed to ensuring that suspects were handled professionally, with integrity and discretion, and in accordance with the law and established procedures.
Earlier today, Anwar said political leaders would be given leeway not to wear the
MACC orange uniform
when brought to court.
He said the matter had been communicated yesterday, adding that those who cooperated with investigations should not necessarily be made to wear the uniform as it could create a different public perception.
"If you want to investigate, investigate first. If there is a case to be brought to court, I leave it to the enforcement authorities to decide what colour uniform should be worn.
"For now, I respect the view because there are people who, I think, cooperate with the investigation, so there is no need for them to be made to wear orange, as it would create a different perception," Anwar said after performing Friday prayers and the funeral prayer at Masjid Bukit Indah today.

Title: Police probe possible gang link in Sungai Lembu shooting
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: Police are probing the possible involvement of gangs in a shooting that injured a 43-year-old man in Machang Bubok yesterday.
Seberang Prai Tengah police chief Assistant Commissioner Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah said investigations were ongoing to determine the motive, identify the suspects and establish whether gangs were involved.
"The case is still under investigation to determine the motive and establish any gang involvement," he said when contacted.
The victim was injured in his right palm after being
shot at a used vehicle workshop
near the Chinese cemetery along Jalan Sungai Lembu about 1.05pm.
Initial investigations found that the victim was approached by two men, who were travelling on a motorcycle.
One of the suspects is believed to have fired a shot at the victim before both men fled the scene.
The victim ran towards the Chinese cemetery to seek safety.
Police have found several items at the scene believed to be linked to the incident.
The case is being investigated under Section 307 of the Penal Code for attempted murder.

Title: Car hits cyclists, killing two best friends in Kota Baru
Article:
KOTA BARU: Two cyclists were killed after they were hit by a car at Km18 of the Kota Baru-Ketereh Highway here this morning.
The two victims died on the spot in the 8.30am crash.
They were identified as Zamrie Rismawadi Mahmet and Nik Zaki Yamani Nik Abdul Aziz, both 49.
The two best friends were believed to have been cycling with seven friends as part of their routine cycling activity during public holidays.
According to a close friend of the victims, Zamrie was cycling in the front lane while Nik Zaki was cycling behind him when they were hit by the car travelling from Kota Baru to Ketereh.
The driver of the car was a man in his 20s.
The two bodies were brought to Raja Perempuan Zainab II Hospital for post-mortems.
Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat confirmed the incident.
He said police were still investigating the cause of the incident.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.

Title: Court rejects Maju Holdings director, wife's DNAA bid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Sessions Court here today dismissed an application by Maju Holdings Sdn Bhd director Tan Sri Abu Sahid Mohamed and his wife for a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA) on charges of criminal breach of trust and money laundering.
Judge Suzana Hussin rejected the application after lawyer Jasbeer Singh, representing Abu Sahid, 75, and Puan Sri Noor Azrina Mohd Azmi, 49, made the application during case management proceedings.
"The court rejects the defence's application, and the prosecution is required to submit a list of witnesses to be called to testify before the court sets the trial date," she said, setting Nov 20 for further case management.
Earlier, Jasbeer sought a DNAA on the grounds that the prosecution had yet to hand over important documents related to the case, despite the charges being brought a year ago.
He said his clients were charged in September last year and seven case mention proceedings had since been held to allow the prosecution to submit the relevant documents.
"The question now is whether the issue concerning the evidence is covered under Section 51A of the Criminal Procedure Code regarding the handing over of documents. Charges should not have been brought if the investigation was still ongoing or incomplete," he said.
However, deputy public prosecutor Nidzuwan Abd Latif told the court that the prosecution would hand over five more volumes of documents after liaising with the relevant authorities and agencies.
He said the documents would be provided before the trial to give the defence sufficient time to prepare.
Abu Sahid faces five charges of misappropriating more than RM458.5 million belonging to the company that had been entrusted to him, involving bank accounts in Taman Tunku and Taman Serdang Perdana, between May 3, 2016 and Oct 21, 2019.
The charges were framed under Section 409 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
He also faces 10 charges of transferring proceeds from unlawful activities amounting to RM116,449,536.12 from his accounts to five people and four construction companies.
In three other money laundering charges, Abu Sahid is alleged to have disposed of proceeds from unlawful activities totalling RM22,802,612.86 by making cash withdrawals through 15 cheques from his account at the same bank between May 4, 2016 and Sept 19, 2018.
Meanwhile, Noor Azrina was charged with receiving proceeds from unlawful activities amounting to
RM67.14 million
through her bank account from an account belonging to Abu Sahid.
The offence was allegedly committed at a bank in Bukit Tunku between March 6, 2017 and Nov 27, 2017.
Abu Sahid's three money laundering charges and Noor Azrina's charge were brought under Section 4(1)(b) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001, punishable under Section 4(1) of the same Act.
A conviction under the section carries a maximum prison term of 15 years and a fine of not less than five times the amount of the proceeds of unlawful activity or RM5 million, whichever is higher.

Title: [UPDATED] King consents to emergency declaration in Serian [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has consented to the declaration of an emergency throughout Serian, Sarawak following worsening haze.
In a statement, the Prime Minister's Office said the decision was made after taking into consideration the advice of the prime minister and the Sarawak premier, as well as relevant agencies, regarding air quality levels in the affected area.
"More effective measures will be taken to protect the health and welfare of affected residents.
"The government will continue to monitor developments from time to time and ensure all necessary measures are implemented promptly, including mitigation measures and the dissemination of health information and advice to the public," it said.
At 2pm today, haze in Serian, Sarawak lingered at hazardous levels, with the Air Pollutant Index (API) reaching 521.
A check on the Department of Environment's (DoE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) website showed Kuching was the only other location to record a hazardous reading, at 311.
Two locations recorded very unhealthy readings — Samarahan (284) and Sri Aman (235).
Meanwhile, 11 locations recorded unhealthy readings: Sarikei (182), Sibu (181), Mukah (177), Bintulu (157), Kota Kinabalu (152), Tawau (151), Samalaju (146), Sandakan (140), Pasir Gudang, Johor (128), Segamat, Johor (115), and Miri (112).
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are categorised as hazardous.
API readings are updated hourly based on data from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide.
Readings above 500 are considered indicative of extremely severe pollution and could trigger immediate emergency action by the authorities, depending on the situation.

Title: Teen drowns off Pantai Klebang, mother mourns family's hope
Article:
MELAKA: "He was our hope to care for his sister, who is also a person with disabilities, but he left us first."
Those were the heartbreaking words of Mazan Jaafar, 51, whose 16-year-old son, Muhammad Arif Daniel Nizamuddin, was found drowned after he went swimming with a friend off Pantai Klebang here two days ago.
Mazan, a general assistant at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Bukit Rambai, said Arif, the youngest of two siblings, had been the family's hope of caring for his older sister, who has Down syndrome.
She said the siblings shared a close bond, with Arif helping to attend to his sister's needs since he was young.
"Arif was our hope and we had hoped he would care for his sister when we are no longer around.
"He was a good, quiet and obedient boy. If we told him not to do something, he would listen. If we gave him permission, he would do it," she said when met at Melaka Hospital today.
Mazan said caring for his sister had been part of Arif's daily routine, including preparing her breakfast before leaving for college.
Even before the tragedy, Arif had collected nasi lemak from his father at work to bring home for his sister.
Mazan said his sister appeared to realise that her brother was gone, repeatedly calling his name after the incident.
"She kept saying, 'Arif, Arif'. They were very close," she said.
Mazan said Arif would usually inform his parents whenever he planned to go out.
"I did not know he had gone there. As far as I knew, he had gone to school.
"When his friend called my husband to tell us what had happened, we were shocked," she said.
Earlier, media reports said Muhammad Arif was believed to have gone missing while swimming with a friend off Pantai Klebang about 3pm.
His
body was found
by fishermen near Pulau Upeh at 7.20pm, following a two-day search and rescue (SAR) operation.
His remains were buried at the Bukit Rambai Muslim Cemetery.
